clue.text: Devise song about film (where stars may be seen)

indicators.note: here the song sits right up against the film, round it in the sense of being next to it in the charade

parts.note: to devise something is to plan it
ET is the classic crossword film, Spielberg's E.T.
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A songwriter is asked to compose a number about a film, with a stargazing aside in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words read like an aside but are the definition, and a plural one: these are the domed buildings where stars are projected.
explanation.definitionFit: Planetaria are buildings with domed ceilings onto which images of the night sky are projected for audiences.

clue.text: Row involving one oddly like a big cat

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the row's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of one are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out in which someone behaves strangely, like a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it means a line of things, and 'oddly' is the anagram signal rather than a description of behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine is the adjective for lions, the big cats, as feline is for cats in general.

clue.text: New worry, finding fastener

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or worry someone

explanation.surface: A fresh concern arises when someone discovers a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a metal spike hammered in to fasten pieces of wood together.

clue.text: Giant squeezing head of Italian painter

indicators.note: squeezing means holding something tightly inside

parts.note: a titan is a giant

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Italian

explanation.surface: A huge figure crushes an Italian painter in a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: TITAN squeezes I, the first letter of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Extremely resolute one-time agent of change

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, here of resolute

parts.note: one-time means former, as in a one-time champion

explanation.surface: A very determined person who used to be a secret agent now pushes for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' looks like a spy picking up 'one-time', but 'agent of change' is the definition; the outer letters of resolute give RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformer campaigns to bring about change and improvement in institutions or society.

clue.text: Scent a wanderer picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a roamer is a wanderer

explanation.surface: A tracker dog follows the smell left by a drifter.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'a roamer' sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell, usually a pleasant one, so it is a synonym of scent.

clue.text: Vindictive move — tell an edited version

indicators.note: an edited version of something has had its parts rearranged and reworked

explanation.surface: Someone tells a doctored version of events as a spiteful move.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, which is the spiteful attitude of a vindictive person.

clue.text: Self-admirer obtained one in east of France

indicators.note: in places the obtained and one letters inside the French word

parts.note: est is French for east
got means obtained
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vain person got a place in eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of France' reads like a region, but it means the French word for east, EST.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is conceited and thinks too highly of themself, so admires their own person.

clue.text: Irrelevant additional intelligence about hallucinatory drug

parts.note: extra means additional

indicators.note: about means going round, so the intelligence word goes around the drug

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A report says more intelligence has come in about a drug that causes hallucinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' suggests spying information, but here it is NOUS, which goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraneous matter is not pertinent to the subject at hand, so it is beside the point.

clue.text: Girl originally from Hebridean island?

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so the first letter of from

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A young woman perhaps comes from a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast; Iona is famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a Scottish female first name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Slender object cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing the last letter, here the final G

parts.note: a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A slim item has been trimmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and slender both describe something with little width or bulk, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Bearing of one stopping aggression on road?

parts.note: a car is what you find on a road

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one goes into the aggression word

parts.note: rage is violent anger or aggression
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone describes the posture of a person who blocks road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a compass direction, but it is the definition in its sense of posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way a person holds their body when standing or walking, which is their bearing or posture.

clue.text: Voice raised in river brawl?

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fight at the riverside involved raised voices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voice raised' reads as shouting, but a falsetto is a voice raised in pitch. The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer uses above his normal range, a voice pitched upwards.

clue.text: Vicious criminal beheaded revenue collector round back of office

indicators.note: round means going around, so the shortened collector surrounds the letter
beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a taxman collects revenue for the government

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of office

explanation.surface: A villain attacks a tax official near the rear of an office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' suits a violent scene, but it removes the T of TAXMAN, leaving AXMAN to go round E, the last letter of office.
explanation.definitionFit: An axeman is a killer who attacks with an axe, so he is a violent criminal.

clue.text: Oddball's party beside dam

indicators.note: beside means placed next to, so the party word follows the dam word here

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An eccentric is holding a party next to a dam.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd, eccentric person, which is what an oddball is too.

clue.text: Communist leader, one with brightly coloured hair

parts.note: a red is a communist
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A communist leader has hair of a vivid colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A redhead is a person with red, ginger or auburn hair, a vivid hair colour.

clue.text: Riddle employed in game

indicators.note: employed means put to use, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzle is used in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed' reads as plain 'used', but it tells you to rearrange IN and GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzling thing or mystery, which is what a riddle is too.

clue.text: Passing first of exams before expiring!

indicators.note: before means the exam letter comes ahead of the rest
the first of a word is its opening letter, here of exams

parts.note: lapsing means expiring, as a lapsed licence has run out

explanation.surface: A student passes the first exam just before a deadline runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like success in exams, but it means time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that is elapsing is going by, so it is passing, as in the passing of the years.

clue.text: Front put up by a fabulous Greek writer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the single letter sits next to the reversed word
put up means raised, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pose is a front, a false appearance

explanation.surface: A Greek author puts on a show of bravado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' reads as marvellous, but it means a writer of fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the fables, such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Unemployed lad primarily tucking into fish

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the letter is put within the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter of lad

explanation.surface: A jobless lad eats some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but it means L goes inside IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle worker has no work to do, so is out of a job.

clue.text: Region in Far East?

indicators.note: in means the answer lies within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a region lies in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or zone, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Before magistrate, prepared for trouble

parts.note: to be up before a magistrate is to appear in court
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Someone appears in court ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is a verb here: to upset someone is to trouble them.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to distress or bother them, which is a sense of trouble as a verb.

clue.text: Item of clothing bloke wrapped round limb

indicators.note: wrapped round means enclosing, so the man's letters go around the limb's

parts.note: a gent is a man, a bloke
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A man winds a piece of clothing around his arm.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloke is everyday British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is any single piece of clothing, such as a shirt or coat.

clue.text: Disinformation demanding serious look, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks whether the words, when spoken, sound like the answer

parts.note: a proper gander is a good long look, gander being British slang for a look

explanation.surface: False reports seem to call for close scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gander is a look, so a proper gander is a thorough one; said in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased or misleading information spread to promote a cause, so it is a form of disinformation.
